summary: You need 135 graduate units, including the core epidemiology and biostatistics sequences, 8 units of research seminars and grant writing (three quarters of EPI 236 and two of EPI 246 among them), 9 units of methods coursework (any 200-level STATS course except STATS 260 also counts), and 9 units of electives in at least three content areas. Every core course except EPI 264 must be letter graded with a B or better. Your advisor checks the 3.0 GPA and that the electives span three areas, and the department records the preliminary written exam at the end of winter of your second year, the oral qualifying exam by the end of autumn of your third year, the defense and the dissertation.

z51kh5vU-text.why: "Epidemiology PhD students must pass the Preliminary Written Exams and the Oral Qualifying Exam before being admitted to candidacy." and "Doctoral students in Epidemiology and Clinical Research must complete and pass the Preliminary Written Exam given around the end of winter term of their second year". The Oral Qualifying Exam ("by the end of autumn quarter of Year 3") is rule ov-epidcr-phd-qual; this rule is the written exam.
